audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's lament over human service, sleepless nights, fleeting life, divine surveillance, Sea/Monster imagery, and the plea to be left alone before death. Sensitive death-language is restrained while preserving the lament.

verses.restored: Is there not hard service for a mortal on earth, and are not his days like the days of a hired worker?

familiar.text: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?

modern.text: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?

original.text: הֲלֹא צָבָ֣א לֶאֱנ֣וֹשׁ על אָ֑רֶץ וְכִימֵ֖י שָׂכִ֣יר יָמָֽיו

verses.restored: Like a servant who pants for shade, and like a hired worker who waits for his wage,

familiar.text: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:

modern.text: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.

original.text: כְּעֶ֥בֶד יִשְׁאַף צֵ֑ל וּ֝כְשָׂכִ֗יר יְקַוֶּ֥ה פָעֳלֽוֹ

verses.restored: so I have been made to inherit months of emptiness, and nights of trouble have been appointed to me.

familiar.text: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

modern.text: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed me.

original.text: כֵּ֤ן הָנְחַ֣לְתִּי לִ֭י יַרְחֵי שָׁ֑וְא וְלֵיל֥וֹת עָ֝מָ֗ל מִנּוּ לִֽי

verses.restored: When I lie down, I say, When shall I rise? But the night stretches on, and I am filled with tossing until dawn.

familiar.text: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

modern.text: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.

original.text: אִם שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מָתַ֣י אָ֭קוּם וּמִדַּד עָ֑רֶב וְשָׂבַ֖עְתִּי נְדֻדִ֣ים עֲדֵי נָֽשֶׁף

verses.restored: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin hardens and breaks open.

familiar.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.

modern.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt; my skin is cracked and festering.

original.text: לָ֘בַ֤שׁ בְּשָׂרִ֣י רִ֭מָּה וגיש עָפָ֑ר עוֹרִ֥י רָ֝גַ֗ע וַיִּמָּאֵֽס

verses.restored: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.

familiar.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

modern.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.

original.text: יָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי אָ֑רֶג וַ֝יִּכְל֗וּ בְּאֶ֣פֶס תִּקְוָֽה

verses.restored: Remember that my life is breath; my eye will not return to see good.

familiar.text: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.

modern.text: Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.

original.text: זְ֭כֹר כִּי ר֣וּחַ חַיָּ֑י לֹא תָשׁ֥וּב עֵ֝ינִ֗י לִרְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב

verses.restored: The eye of the one seeing me will not behold me; your eyes will be on me, but I will be gone.

familiar.text: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.

modern.text: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.

original.text: לֹֽא תְ֭שׁוּרֵנִי עֵ֣ין רֹ֑אִי עֵינֶ֖יךָ בִּ֣י וְאֵינֶֽנִּי

verses.restored: A cloud vanishes and goes away; so the one who goes down to Sheol does not come up.

familiar.text: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.

modern.text: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.

original.text: כָּלָ֣ה עָ֭נָן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ כֵּ֥ן יוֹרֵ֥ד שְׁ֝א֗וֹל לֹ֣א יַעֲלֶֽה

verses.restored: He does not return again to his house, and his place knows him no more.

familiar.text: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

modern.text: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.

original.text: לֹא יָשׁ֣וּב ע֣וֹד לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹא יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקֹמֽוֹ

verses.restored: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth. I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

familiar.text: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

modern.text: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

original.text: גַּם אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: Am I the Sea, or the Sea-Monster, that you set a guard over me?

familiar.text: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

modern.text: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?

original.text: הֲֽיָם אָ֭נִי אִם תַּנִּ֑ין כִּֽי תָשִׂ֖ים עָלַ֣י מִשְׁמָֽר

verses.restored: When I say, My bed will comfort me, my couch will lift my complaint,

familiar.text: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

modern.text: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,

original.text: כִּֽי אָ֭מַרְתִּי תְּנַחֲמֵ֣נִי עַרְשִׂ֑י יִשָּׂ֥א בְ֝שִׂיחִ֗י מִשְׁכָּבִֽי

verses.restored: then you terrify me with dreams and frighten me with visions,

familiar.text: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:

modern.text: then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,

original.text: וְחִתַּתַּ֥נִי בַחֲלֹמ֑וֹת וּֽמֵחֶזְיֹנ֥וֹת תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי

verses.restored: so that my soul chooses an ending; death seems preferable to this body of bones.

familiar.text: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.

modern.text: so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.

original.text: וַתִּבְחַ֣ר מַחֲנָ֣ק נַפְשִׁ֑י מָ֝֗וֶת מֵֽעַצְמוֹתָֽי

verses.restored: I reject it; I will not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are breath.

familiar.text: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.

modern.text: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

original.text: מָ֭אַסְתִּי לֹא לְעֹלָ֣ם אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה חֲדַ֥ל מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי כִּי הֶ֥בֶל יָמָֽי

verses.restored: What is a human, that you make so much of him, and that you set your heart on him,

familiar.text: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

modern.text: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,

original.text: מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: that you inspect him every morning and test him every moment?

familiar.text: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?

modern.text: that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?

original.text: וַתִּפְקְדֶ֥נּוּ לִבְקָרִ֑ים לִ֝רְגָעִ֗ים תִּבְחָנֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone even for a moment?

familiar.text: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

modern.text: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?

original.text: כַּ֭מָּה לֹא תִשְׁעֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי לֹֽא תַ֝רְפֵּ֗נִי עַד בִּלְעִ֥י רֻקִּֽי

verses.restored: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, watcher of humanity? Why have you made me your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?

familiar.text: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?

modern.text: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?

original.text: חָטָ֡אתִי מָ֤ה אֶפְעַ֨ל לָךְ֮ נֹצֵ֪ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם לָ֤מָה שַׂמְתַּ֣נִי לְמִפְגָּ֣ע לָ֑ךְ וָאֶהְיֶ֖ה עָלַ֣י לְמַשָּֽׂא

verses.restored: Why do you not lift away my transgression and pass over my guilt? For now I will lie down in the dust; you will seek me, but I will not be.

familiar.text: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

modern.text: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”

original.text: וּמֶ֤ה לֹא תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֪יר אֶת עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי
